editorial.marketOverview: Friday's shortened session ended with Nasdaq up 2.31%, SOX about 4.7% and Russell 2000 up 1.7%; AP reports Nasdaq gained 6.7% over the week. QQQ repository return was 2.69%, with exact underlying timestamp unverified. Broad participation supports the relief case, but the latest repository model describes mixed chip and mega-cap internals. No weekend cash-market response exists.
editorial.whatChanged: The 13:27 ET repository report retains -24/100, mixed semiconductor and mega-cap internals and positive breadth. Open Watch remains unchanged at 02:31 UTC. Saturday Financial Express corroborates Friday chip leadership, with Micron and Marvell outperforming Nvidia; AP confirms broad weekly gains. Forex.com describes a tentative technical recovery rather than a confirmed bottom. No new market-moving development establishes a changed path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The unchanged -24 model score supports a cautious neutral stance. Historical repository yields of 4.936% and 4.710% imply +22.6 bp without further scaling; WSJ independently reported 4.921% and 4.693%. VXN 33.34 and VIX 23.81 remain timestamp-unverified dashboard values. Reuters confirms Friday Brent $95.44 and WTI $83.08 settlements, with Brent up about 3% weekly. MarketWatch reported 99% December hike probability Friday, not a live weekend reading.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday tests Friday's relief under normal liquidity after Sunday's OPEC+ decision, which Reuters expects to leave first-quarter targets unchanged. Tuesday manufacturing and labor releases can reprice rates; Marvell and Credo earnings after close could shape Wednesday chip trading. Wednesday ADP and labor tightness data add rate sensitivity. Friday payrolls and December 8–9 Fed meeting remain outside the horizon.
editorial.bullCase: A sustained positive SOX/QQQ relative return under normal liquidity, broad participation and easing yields would offset the weaker model score. Constructive semiconductor guidance and lower oil supply risk would reinforce the case.
editorial.bearCase: A negative model score and elevated yields leave the rally vulnerable to a reversal in chip leadership, narrower breadth or oil supply pressure. A 10Y move above 5% would strengthen the bearish case, particularly if volatility rises. None of these prospective triggers has been observed this weekend.
editorial.watchNext: Watch the official OPEC+ decision, Sunday futures reopening and Monday matched-time equity, rates and volatility observations. Recheck Tuesday macro and chip earnings schedules and Wednesday employment data. Treat weekend news impact as prospective until markets reopen.
